Transfer to the airport in the morning for your flight to La Paz. The transfer time depends on the flight selected. Airfare is payable separately. The rest of the day is devoted to the ancient civilisation of Tiwanaku and Lake Titicaca.

The ruins of Tiwanaku lie in the Andes and are among the most important pre-Columbian archaeological sites in South America. The civilisation’s history dates back to around AD 400. At the site, you will see the Gateway of the Sun, the Kalasasaya Temple, the Akapana Pyramid and other structures. After the visit, have lunch at Taypi Uta, a local restaurant.

Continue to Huatajata on the shore of Lake Titicaca. The programme includes the Raíces Andinas eco-village, the Altiplano Museum, an artisan village, clay igloos and exhibits on the Uru-Chipaya people. You will meet the Limachi family, whose members helped build expedition vessels including Ra II, which crossed the Atlantic, and Tigris. Vicuñas, llamas, alpacas and suris can be seen nearby.

In the evening, an audiovisual presentation introduces the Mystical World of the Kallawaya. Kallawaya practitioner Tata Benjo will give a traditional blessing and read coca leaves. After dark, visit the Alajpacha Observatory to learn about Andean cosmology and see the constellations of the southern sky. Dinner and overnight at Inca Utama Hotel & Cultural Center.

The day takes you from the archaeology of Tiwanaku to life on the shores of Lake Titicaca, the crafts and wildlife of the Altiplano, and an evening exploring traditional medicine and Andean ideas about the sky. It brings together several layers of Bolivian culture, from ancient stone complexes to the people who live in the highlands today.
